nodes.label: Sharper Thinking
nodes.full_label: Sharper Thinking
nodes.catchy_title: Can You Train Better Judgment?
nodes.summary: Improving your thinking and analytical skills is less about becoming “cleverer” in the abstract and more about building habits that make your judgement slower where it should be slower, clearer where it is muddled, and better tested against evidence.

nodes.label: Active Learning
nodes.full_label: Why Rereading Is Not Enough | Improving Your Think
nodes.catchy_title: Why Rereading Is Not Enough
nodes.summary: Analytical skill grows faster when people retrieve, explain, apply, and test ideas rather than merely reread them.

nodes.label: Explain
nodes.full_label: The Missing Step You Notice When Explaining | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Active Learning
nodes.catchy_title: The Missing Step You Notice When Explaining
nodes.summary: Explaining each step in your own words makes hidden assumptions, weak links and misconceptions easier to notice.

nodes.label: Predict
nodes.full_label: Predict First, Then Let Evidence Correct You | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Active Learning
nodes.catchy_title: Predict First, Then Let Evidence Correct You
nodes.summary: Making a prediction before checking the answer turns passive reading into a comparison between expectation and evidence.

nodes.label: Recall
nodes.full_label: Can You Explain It Without Looking? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Active Learning
nodes.catchy_title: Can You Explain It Without Looking?
nodes.summary: Closing the source and reconstructing ideas from memory exposes the gap between familiar-looking notes and usable knowledge.

nodes.label: Testing
nodes.full_label: Why Tests Can Teach Better Than Review | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Active Learning
nodes.catchy_title: Why Tests Can Teach Better Than Review
nodes.summary: Practice tests improve thinking because answering from memory strengthens recall and reveals mistakes before they matter.

nodes.label: Transfer
nodes.full_label: Can the Idea Survive a New Example? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Active Learning
nodes.catchy_title: Can the Idea Survive a New Example?
nodes.summary: Applying a concept to a new case tests whether understanding survives beyond the example that first taught it.

nodes.label: Work Rehearsal
nodes.full_label: Training That Rehearses the Real Decision | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Active Learning
nodes.catchy_title: Training That Rehearses the Real Decision
nodes.summary: Workplace learning becomes more useful when teams practise the judgments they will later need under real pressure.

nodes.label: Alternatives
nodes.full_label: What Else Could Explain This? | Improving Your Think
nodes.catchy_title: What Else Could Explain This?
nodes.summary: A strong explanation is not just plausible; it has survived comparison with serious alternatives.

nodes.label: A Sudden Fall In Sales
nodes.full_label: Is Demand Down or Data Broken? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Alternative Explanat
nodes.catchy_title: Is Demand Down or Data Broken?
nodes.summary: A revenue change is easier to interpret when analytics, payment data, traffic, refunds, and channel comparisons tell the same story.

nodes.label: Accident Chains
nodes.full_label: Why First Causes Miss the Chain | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Alternative Explanat
nodes.catchy_title: Why First Causes Miss the Chain
nodes.summary: Serious accident inquiries show why visible first causes often give way to chains of mechanical, human, organizational, and environmental factors.

nodes.label: Competing Hypotheses
nodes.full_label: Put Your Explanations in Competition | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Alternative Explanat
nodes.catchy_title: Put Your Explanations in Competition
nodes.summary: Listing hypotheses side by side helps reveal which explanation has the least serious evidence against it.

nodes.label: Control Groups
nodes.full_label: Did Training Work, or Did the Task Change? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Alternative Explanat
nodes.catchy_title: Did Training Work, or Did the Task Change?
nodes.summary: Performance gains are not strong evidence for training until rival explanations such as easier tasks or changing conditions are tested.

nodes.label: Late Replies
nodes.full_label: What Else Could Silence Mean? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Alternative Explanat
nodes.catchy_title: What Else Could Silence Mean?
nodes.summary: A late message can feel personal, but the same silence may come from travel, stress, uncertainty, illness, or simple oversight.

nodes.label: Weak Evidence
nodes.full_label: Does This Evidence Really Pick a Side? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Alternative Explanat
nodes.catchy_title: Does This Evidence Really Pick a Side?
nodes.summary: A fact can fit your favorite story without doing much to rule out serious rivals.

nodes.label: Argument Maps
nodes.full_label: Can Mapping an Argument Improve It? | Improving Your Think
nodes.catchy_title: Can Mapping an Argument Improve It?
nodes.summary: Argument maps turn conclusions, reasons, objections, and assumptions into a visible structure that can be tested.

nodes.label: Assumptions
nodes.full_label: The Missing Premise That Carries the Argument | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Argument Mapping
nodes.catchy_title: The Missing Premise That Carries the Argument
nodes.summary: Argument maps expose the unstated premises that often decide whether a conclusion really follows.

nodes.label: Decision Claims
nodes.full_label: What Is Your Map Really Trying to Prove? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Argument Mapping
nodes.catchy_title: What Is Your Map Really Trying to Prove?
nodes.summary: Starting with a complete decision claim keeps an argument map focused on what is actually being defended.

nodes.label: Evidence Gaps
nodes.full_label: What Your Decision Map Says to Check Next | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Argument Mapping
nodes.catchy_title: What Your Decision Map Says to Check Next
nodes.summary: Mapping a choice reveals which facts still need checking before confidence is justified.

nodes.label: Map Types
nodes.full_label: Why Argument Maps Are Not Mind Maps | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Argument Mapping
nodes.catchy_title: Why Argument Maps Are Not Mind Maps
nodes.summary: Mind maps help association, but argument maps show which claims support, weaken, or depend on each other.

nodes.label: Objections
nodes.full_label: Where Does the Objection Actually Land? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Argument Mapping
nodes.catchy_title: Where Does the Objection Actually Land?
nodes.summary: A good map shows whether an objection weakens one branch, a hidden inference, or the entire claim.

nodes.label: Practice
nodes.full_label: Why One Argument Map Is Not Enough | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Argument Mapping
nodes.catchy_title: Why One Argument Map Is Not Enough
nodes.summary: The strongest evidence for argument mapping comes from repeated practice with feedback, not from drawing one diagram once.

nodes.label: Calibration
nodes.full_label: Is Your Confidence Matched to Evidence? | Improving Your Think
nodes.catchy_title: Is Your Confidence Matched to Evidence?
nodes.summary: Recording predictions with confidence levels turns judgment into a feedback loop instead of a private feeling.

nodes.label: Brier Scores
nodes.full_label: A Simple Scorecard for Forecasting Skill | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Confidence Calibrati
nodes.catchy_title: A Simple Scorecard for Forecasting Skill
nodes.summary: Brier scores give prediction journals a simple way to compare stated probabilities with what actually happened.

nodes.label: Good Judgment
nodes.full_label: What Superforecasting Teaches Everyday Thinkers | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Confidence Calibrati
nodes.catchy_title: What Superforecasting Teaches Everyday Thinkers
nodes.summary: The Good Judgment Project shows how explicit probabilities, feedback, updating, and scoring can improve real-world judgement.

nodes.label: Miss Reviews
nodes.full_label: When a Wrong Forecast Was Still Reasonable | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Confidence Calibrati
nodes.catchy_title: When a Wrong Forecast Was Still Reasonable
nodes.summary: Missed forecasts are most useful when the review separates bad evidence, bad framing, slow updates, and reasonable uncertainty.

nodes.label: Probability Words
nodes.full_label: Why Probably Is Not Precise Enough | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Confidence Calibrati
nodes.catchy_title: Why Probably Is Not Precise Enough
nodes.summary: Numbers make confidence testable in a way that words like likely, doubtful, or probably cannot.

nodes.label: Scorable Questions
nodes.full_label: Can Your Forecast Actually Be Scored? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Confidence Calibrati
nodes.catchy_title: Can Your Forecast Actually Be Scored?
nodes.summary: A good prediction journal starts with questions that are specific enough to resolve and narrow enough to teach you something.

nodes.label: What To Predict
nodes.full_label: The Predictions Worth Writing Down | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Confidence Calibrati
nodes.catchy_title: The Predictions Worth Writing Down
nodes.summary: The most useful journal entries are concrete, repeated predictions about decisions where better calibration would change behavior.

nodes.label: Causation
nodes.full_label: Does the Evidence Show a Cause? | Improving Your Think
nodes.catchy_title: Does the Evidence Show a Cause?
nodes.summary: Analytical thinking improves when people ask whether evidence really supports a cause or only shows a pattern.

nodes.label: App Scores
nodes.full_label: Does the App Raise Scores, or Track Motivation? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Correlation Causatio
nodes.catchy_title: Does the App Raise Scores, or Track Motivation?
nodes.summary: Higher scores among revision app users may reflect study habits and motivation as much as the app itself.

nodes.label: Berkeley Data
nodes.full_label: When the Combined Data Tells the Wrong Story | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Correlation Causatio
nodes.catchy_title: When the Combined Data Tells the Wrong Story
nodes.summary: The Berkeley admissions example shows how an overall pattern can change when the data are split into meaningful groups.

nodes.label: Fair Tests
nodes.full_label: Why Randomised Trials Make Causal Claims Stronger | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Correlation Causatio
nodes.catchy_title: Why Randomised Trials Make Causal Claims Stronger
nodes.summary: Random assignment helps test causal claims by making groups more comparable than ordinary observation usually allows.

nodes.label: Hidden Causes
nodes.full_label: When a Third Factor Creates the Pattern | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Correlation Causatio
nodes.catchy_title: When a Third Factor Creates the Pattern
nodes.summary: The ice cream and drowning example shows how a hidden third factor can make a harmless pattern look causal.

nodes.label: Onboarding Bias
nodes.full_label: Did Onboarding Help, or Did Motivated Customers Join? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Correlation Causatio
nodes.catchy_title: Did Onboarding Help, or Did Motivated Customers Join?
nodes.summary: Customers who attend onboarding may spend more because they were already more motivated, not because onboarding changed them.

nodes.label: Sleep Claims
nodes.full_label: Does Short Sleep Cause Risk, or Signal It? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Correlation Causatio
nodes.catchy_title: Does Short Sleep Cause Risk, or Signal It?
nodes.summary: Sleep and mortality claims need timing, pathways, and rival explanations before a correlation becomes credible advice.

nodes.label: Change Mind
nodes.full_label: What Evidence Would Change Your Mind? | Improving Your Think
nodes.catchy_title: What Evidence Would Change Your Mind?
nodes.summary: Asking what evidence would change your conclusion protects against reasoning that cannot be tested.

nodes.label: Confidence Updates
nodes.full_label: Why Changing Your Mind Can Mean Changing Your Confidence | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Change My Mind
nodes.catchy_title: Why Changing Your Mind Can Mean Changing Your Confidence
nodes.summary: Evidence often justifies smaller confidence shifts rather than dramatic reversals.

nodes.label: Disconfirming Evidence
nodes.full_label: Why Contradictory Evidence Is More Useful Than More Proof | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Change My Mind
nodes.catchy_title: Why Contradictory Evidence Is More Useful Than More Proof
nodes.summary: The strongest test of a belief often comes from evidence that could prove it wrong.

nodes.label: Premortems
nodes.full_label: Can a Premortem Reveal When You Should Reconsider? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Change My Mind
nodes.catchy_title: Can a Premortem Reveal When You Should Reconsider?
nodes.summary: Imagining a future failure helps identify early warning signs before a decision becomes difficult to reverse.

nodes.label: Review Triggers
nodes.full_label: How Review Triggers Make Changing Course Easier | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Change My Mind
nodes.catchy_title: How Review Triggers Make Changing Course Easier
nodes.summary: Predefined review triggers help teams revisit decisions without treating every setback as a crisis.

nodes.label: Revision Rules
nodes.full_label: What Would Actually Make You Change Your Mind? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Change My Mind
nodes.catchy_title: What Would Actually Make You Change Your Mind?
nodes.summary: Clear revision conditions make it harder to ignore evidence that challenges your current view.

nodes.label: Wason
nodes.full_label: What the 2 4 6 Experiment Teaches About Better Decisions | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Change My Mind
nodes.catchy_title: What the 2 4 6 Experiment Teaches About Better Decisions
nodes.summary: A classic psychology experiment shows why people often test ideas by confirming rather than challenging them.

nodes.label: Claims
nodes.full_label: What Is the Claim Really Based On? | Improving Your Think
nodes.catchy_title: What Is the Claim Really Based On?
nodes.summary: Good analysis depends on separating what is being claimed from the evidence and assumptions that supposedly support it.

nodes.label: Anecdotes
nodes.full_label: When Does One Example Actually Prove Anything? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Claims Evidence Assu
nodes.catchy_title: When Does One Example Actually Prove Anything?
nodes.summary: A single vivid story can be a useful clue, but it rarely proves a broad claim unless it is typical and well connected.

nodes.label: Late Replies
nodes.full_label: Do Late Replies Really Show Disrespect? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Claims Evidence Assu
nodes.catchy_title: Do Late Replies Really Show Disrespect?
nodes.summary: Late messages may feel personal, but the argument from delay to disrespect depends on assumptions about intent, norms, and context.

nodes.label: Policy Timing
nodes.full_label: Did the Policy Fail, or Just Come First? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Claims Evidence Assu
nodes.catchy_title: Did the Policy Fail, or Just Come First?
nodes.summary: A bad outcome after a policy change is not enough to show the policy failed unless competing causes are ruled out.

nodes.label: Supplements
nodes.full_label: Did the Supplement Work, or Did You Recover? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Claims Evidence Assu
nodes.catchy_title: Did the Supplement Work, or Did You Recover?
nodes.summary: Feeling better after taking a supplement can matter personally, but it does not by itself prove the supplement caused the improvement.

nodes.label: Warrants
nodes.full_label: The Hidden Bridge in Every Argument | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Claims Evidence Assu
nodes.catchy_title: The Hidden Bridge in Every Argument
nodes.summary: The warrant is the quiet bridge between evidence and claim, and finding it often reveals where the disagreement really sits.

nodes.label: Work Complaints
nodes.full_label: Are Three Complaints Enough to Blame the Software? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Claims Evidence Assu
nodes.catchy_title: Are Three Complaints Enough to Blame the Software?
nodes.summary: Three frustrated colleagues may reveal a real software problem, or they may reflect a narrow slice of the team's experience.

nodes.label: Confirmation Bias
nodes.full_label: Are You Protecting Your First Answer? | Improving Your Think
nodes.catchy_title: Are You Protecting Your First Answer?
nodes.summary: Confirmation bias makes people seek support for a first answer instead of seriously testing alternatives.

nodes.label: First Answer
nodes.full_label: Why the First Answer Starts Winning | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Confirmation Bias
nodes.catchy_title: Why the First Answer Starts Winning
nodes.summary: A promising first answer can turn into a protected story when relief, identity, or social cost makes contrary evidence feel threatening.

nodes.label: Health Doubt
nodes.full_label: When Symptoms Seem to Confirm Your Fear | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Confirmation Bias
nodes.catchy_title: When Symptoms Seem to Confirm Your Fear
nodes.summary: Fear or hope can make one explanation feel obvious, so serious health decisions need clear counterevidence questions and second-opinion triggers.

nodes.label: Job Regret
nodes.full_label: What Would Make This Job Regrettable? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Confirmation Bias
nodes.catchy_title: What Would Make This Job Regrettable?
nodes.summary: Before accepting or staying in a role, the regret question forces hidden warnings into view before career momentum takes over.

nodes.label: Red Flags
nodes.full_label: Is This Patience or Evidence Avoidance? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Confirmation Bias
nodes.catchy_title: Is This Patience or Evidence Avoidance?
nodes.summary: Generosity becomes risky when repeated behavior would look obvious in a friend's relationship but complicated in your own.

nodes.label: Rival Test
nodes.full_label: The Test Your Favorite Story Needs | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Confirmation Bias
nodes.catchy_title: The Test Your Favorite Story Needs
nodes.summary: A useful test does not just ask whether your favorite explanation can survive; it asks what would separate it from a serious rival.

nodes.label: Search Trap
nodes.full_label: When Research Becomes a Search Trap | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Confirmation Bias
nodes.catchy_title: When Research Becomes a Search Trap
nodes.summary: Searching only for reasons to proceed can make a decision feel researched while hiding the strongest reasons it might fail.

nodes.label: Critical Thinking
nodes.full_label: What Does Critical Thinking Really Mean? | Improving Your Think
nodes.catchy_title: What Does Critical Thinking Really Mean?
nodes.summary: Critical thinking is purposeful, self-regulated judgment, not just scepticism or having sharper opinions.

nodes.label: Clear Question
nodes.full_label: What Question Are You Really Answering? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Purposeful Judgment
nodes.catchy_title: What Question Are You Really Answering?
nodes.summary: A clear question keeps critical thinking from becoming endless commentary and makes evidence easier to test.

nodes.label: Critical Trust
nodes.full_label: Is Doubt Helping or Just Hardening? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Purposeful Judgment
nodes.catchy_title: Is Doubt Helping or Just Hardening?
nodes.summary: Critical thinking is not automatic distrust; it means matching trust to the quality of the reasons available.

nodes.label: Delphi Standards
nodes.full_label: What Counts as a Good Critical Judgement? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Purposeful Judgment
nodes.catchy_title: What Counts as a Good Critical Judgement?
nodes.summary: The Delphi Report gives critical thinking a practical standard: interpretation, analysis, evaluation, inference, and explanation.

nodes.label: Remote Work
nodes.full_label: Are Remote Workers Really Less Productive? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Purposeful Judgment
nodes.catchy_title: Are Remote Workers Really Less Productive?
nodes.summary: The remote-work productivity debate shows why critical thinkers define terms, compare evidence, and test alternative explanations.

nodes.label: Self Checks
nodes.full_label: How to Catch Your Own Double Standards | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Purposeful Judgment
nodes.catchy_title: How to Catch Your Own Double Standards
nodes.summary: Self-regulation turns critical thinking inward by asking whether your own standards are fair, consistent, and evidence-led.

nodes.label: Thinking Habits
nodes.full_label: Why Smart People Still Need Thinking Habits | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Purposeful Judgment
nodes.catchy_title: Why Smart People Still Need Thinking Habits
nodes.summary: Critical-thinking skills matter most when dispositions like truth-seeking, open-mindedness, and systematicity make people use them.

nodes.label: Decision Stakes
nodes.full_label: How Much Thinking Is Enough? | Improving Your Think
nodes.catchy_title: How Much Thinking Is Enough?
nodes.summary: The amount of analysis should match the cost, uncertainty, and reversibility of the decision.

nodes.label: Decision Notes
nodes.full_label: Write the Reasoning Before You Commit | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Decision Stakes
nodes.catchy_title: Write the Reasoning Before You Commit
nodes.summary: A short decision note can capture assumptions, tradeoffs, regret risks, and review points before a hard-to-reverse choice is made.

nodes.label: One Way Doors
nodes.full_label: Which Decisions Deserve Slower Thinking? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Decision Stakes
nodes.catchy_title: Which Decisions Deserve Slower Thinking?
nodes.summary: Some choices deserve extra friction because the damage is serious, hard to undo, or likely to reshape later options.

nodes.label: Paralysis
nodes.full_label: Why Small Choices Can Steal Big Attention | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Decision Stakes
nodes.catchy_title: Why Small Choices Can Steal Big Attention
nodes.summary: Overthinking small reversible choices can waste attention that would be better saved for decisions with real downside.

nodes.label: Premortems
nodes.full_label: Imagine Failure Before It Happens | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Decision Stakes
nodes.catchy_title: Imagine Failure Before It Happens
nodes.summary: A premortem helps people notice plausible reasons a decision could fail before commitment makes them harder to discuss.

nodes.label: Shared Risk
nodes.full_label: Who Pays If This Goes Wrong? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Decision Stakes
nodes.catchy_title: Who Pays If This Goes Wrong?
nodes.summary: A decision deserves more care when other people bear the risk, even if it feels easy or routine to the decision-maker.

nodes.label: Two Way Tests
nodes.full_label: When Is Acting the Better Analysis? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Decision Stakes
nodes.catchy_title: When Is Acting the Better Analysis?
nodes.summary: Reversible choices often improve faster through small experiments than through long private debate.

nodes.label: Deliberate Practice
nodes.full_label: Why Experience Alone Does Not Fix Thinking | Improving Your Think
nodes.catchy_title: Why Experience Alone Does Not Fix Thinking
nodes.summary: Better judgment comes from targeted practice with feedback, not simply from years of unexamined experience.

nodes.label: Alternatives
nodes.full_label: What else could explain this? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Deliberate Practice
nodes.catchy_title: What else could explain this?
nodes.summary: Generating rival explanations slows the jump from a plausible first story to a confident but poorly tested conclusion.

nodes.label: Argument Maps
nodes.full_label: Can argument maps expose weak reasoning? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Deliberate Practice
nodes.catchy_title: Can argument maps expose weak reasoning?
nodes.summary: Argument maps turn messy prose into visible claims, reasons and assumptions so weak links can be fixed instead of vaguely criticised.

nodes.label: Calibration
nodes.full_label: How sure should you really be? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Deliberate Practice
nodes.catchy_title: How sure should you really be?
nodes.summary: Calibration practice teaches people to attach numbers to uncertainty, check outcomes, and notice when confidence outruns accuracy.

nodes.label: Error Logs
nodes.full_label: What kind of wrong was it? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Deliberate Practice
nodes.catchy_title: What kind of wrong was it?
nodes.summary: An error log turns being wrong into useful data by naming the kind of mistake and the correction to practise next.

nodes.label: Faded Prompts
nodes.full_label: When should reasoning prompts disappear? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Deliberate Practice
nodes.catchy_title: When should reasoning prompts disappear?
nodes.summary: Faded prompts help learners practise a reasoning move repeatedly until they can use it without step-by-step support.

nodes.label: Prediction Logs
nodes.full_label: Why prediction logs make thinking measurable | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Deliberate Practice
nodes.catchy_title: Why prediction logs make thinking measurable
nodes.summary: Prediction logs make reasoning practice measurable by recording forecasts, evidence, updates and results in one place.

nodes.label: Feedback
nodes.full_label: How Do You Learn From Wrong Calls? | Improving Your Think
nodes.catchy_title: How Do You Learn From Wrong Calls?
nodes.summary: Feedback turns reasoning from a one-off performance into a process that can improve after errors.

nodes.label: Confident Errors
nodes.full_label: Why Confident Mistakes Can Teach More | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Feedback Loops Judgm
nodes.catchy_title: Why Confident Mistakes Can Teach More
nodes.summary: Being confidently wrong can be useful when corrective feedback clearly shows the gap between belief and reality.

nodes.label: Decision Journals
nodes.full_label: Can a Decision Journal Make You Less Foolable? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Feedback Loops Judgm
nodes.catchy_title: Can a Decision Journal Make You Less Foolable?
nodes.summary: A short decision journal freezes what you knew, expected and believed before the outcome rewrites the story.

nodes.label: Outcome Bias
nodes.full_label: Was It Skill, Luck or Bad Feedback? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Feedback Loops Judgm
nodes.catchy_title: Was It Skill, Luck or Bad Feedback?
nodes.summary: Good outcomes can reward bad reasoning, while bad outcomes can punish sound decisions that simply ran into bad luck.

nodes.label: Probability Calls
nodes.full_label: Why Vague Predictions Do Not Teach Much | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Feedback Loops Judgm
nodes.catchy_title: Why Vague Predictions Do Not Teach Much
nodes.summary: Putting a number on a prediction turns fuzzy confidence into something that can be checked, scored and improved.

nodes.label: Team Reviews
nodes.full_label: When Team Reviews Actually Improve Judgement | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Feedback Loops Judgm
nodes.catchy_title: When Team Reviews Actually Improve Judgement
nodes.summary: A good after-action review asks what was expected, what happened, why it differed and what should change next time.

nodes.label: Weak Feedback
nodes.full_label: When Experience Makes Judgement Worse | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Feedback Loops Judgm
nodes.catchy_title: When Experience Makes Judgement Worse
nodes.summary: In noisy or delayed settings, repeated experience can build confidence without producing reliable learning.

nodes.label: First Answers
nodes.full_label: Why First Answers Feel So Convincing | Improving Your Think
nodes.catchy_title: Why First Answers Feel So Convincing
nodes.summary: The Cognitive Reflection Test shows how tempting first answers can feel right before they have been checked.

nodes.label: Backwards Test
nodes.full_label: A Quick Test for Answers That Feel Obvious | Improving Your Think Da 4710 First Answer Traps
nodes.catchy_title: A Quick Test for Answers That Feel Obvious
nodes.summary: Putting a first answer back into the original problem is a fast way to catch answers that feel right but violate a condition.

nodes.label: Bat and Ball
nodes.full_label: Why the 10 Cent Answer Feels Right | Improving Your Think Da 4710 First Answer Traps
nodes.catchy_title: Why the 10 Cent Answer Feels Right
nodes.summary: The famous bat-and-ball puzzle shows why an answer can fit the total while failing the exact condition that makes it correct.

nodes.label: False Fluency
nodes.full_label: Why Easy Answers Can Feel More True | Improving Your Think Da 4710 First Answer Traps
nodes.catchy_title: Why Easy Answers Can Feel More True
nodes.summary: Answers that come easily can feel more trustworthy than they deserve, especially when surface fit hides a failed constraint.

nodes.label: Familiarity
nodes.full_label: When Knowing the Answer Becomes the Trap | Improving Your Think Da 4710 First Answer Traps
nodes.catchy_title: When Knowing the Answer Becomes the Trap
nodes.summary: Knowing the classic CRT answers may raise scores without proving that someone has learned to catch new first-answer traps.

nodes.label: Lily Pads
nodes.full_label: The Growth Puzzle That Punishes Straight Lines | Improving Your Think Da 4710 First Answer Traps
nodes.catchy_title: The Growth Puzzle That Punishes Straight Lines
nodes.summary: The lily-pad question makes a linear guess feel natural even though doubling growth requires reasoning backwards from the final day.

nodes.label: Numeracy Limits
nodes.full_label: Does the CRT Measure Reflection or Math? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 First Answer Traps
nodes.catchy_title: Does the CRT Measure Reflection or Math?
nodes.summary: CRT scores can reflect calculation skill as well as reflective thinking, so a low score is not a clean diagnosis of poor reasoning.

nodes.label: Health Claims
nodes.full_label: How Should You Judge Health Advice? | Improving Your Think
nodes.catchy_title: How Should You Judge Health Advice?
nodes.summary: Health advice needs careful evidence checks because confident claims can mix real findings with overreach.

nodes.label: Diet Claims
nodes.full_label: Did the Diet Cause the Benefit? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Health Claim Skeptic
nodes.catchy_title: Did the Diet Cause the Benefit?
nodes.summary: Nutrition headlines often turn population patterns into personal rules before confounding and comparison groups are handled properly.

nodes.label: Markers
nodes.full_label: When Better Numbers Do Not Mean Better Health | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Health Claim Skeptic
nodes.catchy_title: When Better Numbers Do Not Mean Better Health
nodes.summary: A number moving in the right direction is not the same as fewer illnesses, longer life, better function, or less suffering.

nodes.label: Risk Numbers
nodes.full_label: What Does a 50 Percent Risk Cut Mean? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Health Claim Skeptic
nodes.catchy_title: What Does a 50 Percent Risk Cut Mean?
nodes.summary: A dramatic percentage can hide a tiny real-world difference unless the baseline risk and time period are made clear.

nodes.label: Screening
nodes.full_label: Does Early Detection Always Help? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Health Claim Skeptic
nodes.catchy_title: Does Early Detection Always Help?
nodes.summary: Early detection can help, but screening claims need absolute benefit, false positives, overdiagnosis, and mortality outcomes in view.

nodes.label: Supplements
nodes.full_label: When Supplement Claims Outrun the Evidence | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Health Claim Skeptic
nodes.catchy_title: When Supplement Claims Outrun the Evidence
nodes.summary: Supplement labels often sound scientific, but the real test is whether human studies show meaningful benefits and tracked harms.

nodes.label: Testimonials
nodes.full_label: Why Feeling Better Is Not Proof | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Health Claim Skeptic
nodes.catchy_title: Why Feeling Better Is Not Proof
nodes.summary: Personal improvement stories can be sincere and still fail to show that a product, routine, or treatment caused the change.

nodes.label: Humility
nodes.full_label: How Do You Stay Open Without Drifting? | Improving Your Think
nodes.catchy_title: How Do You Stay Open Without Drifting?
nodes.summary: Good thinking is not doubting everything; it is being willing to revise beliefs when the evidence changes.

nodes.label: Confidence
nodes.full_label: How Confident Should You Really Be? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Intellectual Humilit
nodes.catchy_title: How Confident Should You Really Be?
nodes.summary: Good judgement improves when confidence is scaled to the quality, independence and directness of the evidence behind a claim.

nodes.label: Core Beliefs
nodes.full_label: Why Some Beliefs Resist Revision | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Intellectual Humilit

nodes.catchy_title: Can a Checklist Make Better Thinking Show Up?

nodes.catchy_title: Can Bias Training Survive Real Life?

nodes.label: Domain Knowledge

nodes.catchy_title: Why Thinking Skills Still Need Knowledge
nodes.summary: General reasoning prompts work best when paired with enough background knowledge to know what counts as evidence in the situation.

nodes.label: Near vs Far

nodes.catchy_title: How Far Can a Thinking Skill Travel?
nodes.summary: Near transfer is easier than far transfer because the new situation shares more visible cues with the original practice.

nodes.label: Outcomes
nodes.full_label: Does Better Thinking Change Real Choices? | Improving Your Think Da 4710 Real World Transfer
nodes.catchy_title: Does Better Thinking Change Real Choices?
nodes.summary: The most useful test of thinking instruction is whether people handle new decisions differently, not whether they can define concepts.

nodes.label: Transfer Gap

nodes.catchy_title: Why Good Thinking Lessons Do Not Stick
